card.occupation: Senior pharmacy technician at a large NHS hospital in Nottingham. She runs the medicines reconciliation side on two medical wards and supervises a small team of junior technicians and assistants. She works full-time, about 37.5 hours on paper and nearer 40 in practice, mostly days with the odd late shift and a weekend on rota.
card.education_detail: She did GCSEs and A-levels in Biology, Chemistry and English at a comprehensive and sixth form in Derby. She started a Biomedical Science degree and left after the first year because she didn't enjoy it and felt guilty about the student loan. She worked in a high-street chemist, then got a trainee pharmacy technician post and completed the BTEC/NVQ Level 3 in Pharmaceutical Science. She registered with the GPhC in her mid-twenties and has since done an accredited checking technician qualification.
card.household: She lives with her husband Rob, 41, an electrician who works for a small local firm. They've been married nine years and have no children. They have a semi-detached 1930s house with a long narrow garden, and an elderly rescue greyhound called Biscuit. Her parents live about fifteen minutes away in Spondon. Her younger brother lives in Leicester with his partner and two little ones, and Gemma is a very hands-on auntie.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Derby to a working-class family. Her dad was a fitter at a Rolls-Royce supplier and her mum was a school dinner lady, then a teaching assistant. She was christened but isn't religious and doesn't really think about it, though she likes a carol service at Christmas for the singing. She is very rooted in the area and has never seriously considered moving away. Her friends are mostly from school, from work, and from the dog-walking crowd.
card.professional_persona: She is the dependable one on the team. She double-checks things without being asked and is the person people come to when a discharge prescription looks wrong. She is careful, methodical and slightly anxious about errors, and she takes it personally if something slips through. She is good with junior staff and patient with them, explaining things twice without making them feel stupid. She hates office politics and won't badmouth colleagues, even ones who annoy her. She is quietly proud of her job but tends to undersell it, often saying 'I'm just a tech' when people assume she's a pharmacist.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive sense. She walks Biscuit every day, usually along the Erewash Canal towpath, and does a parkrun at Long Eaton most Saturdays. She's been doing it for three years and is pleased to be just under 30 minutes now. Rob follows Derby County and she'll go to the odd match with him, mainly for the atmosphere and the pie. She did a Couch to 5K during the first lockdown and kept it up.
card.arts_persona: She reads crime fiction and cosy mysteries, mostly on a Kindle in bed. She watches a lot of telly with Rob: British crime dramas, Bake Off, and anything with a detective. She went to see a touring musical at the Theatre Royal in Nottingham for a friend's birthday and loved it more than she expected. She does a bit of cross-stitch, which is how she unwinds after a stressful shift, and has framed a few pieces for family.
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK holidays: a cottage in the Peak District or North Norfolk with the dog, and a long weekend in York or Whitby. She and Rob do one week abroad most years, usually somewhere easy like Mallorca, Crete or the Algarve, booked well in advance with everything checked twice. She gets a bit nervous about flying and airports but is fine once she's there. Her bucket list trip is the Northern Lights in Norway, which she keeps saying they'll do 'when we've saved up'.
card.culinary_persona: She is a solid, practical home cook. She batch-cooks on her days off: chilli, bolognese and a chicken casserole, frozen in labelled tubs. Sunday dinner at her mum's is a fixture about twice a month. She calls the evening meal 'tea' at home but says 'dinner' at work without thinking about it. A cob with a bacon or sausage is her weekend treat, and she likes a Friday chippy tea. She is trying to bring more vegetarian meals in, with mixed success because Rob is suspicious of lentils.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog along the canal
watching detective dramas and Bake Off
pottering in the garden, mainly tomatoes and sweet peas
days out at National Trust places like Calke Abbey and Kedleston
being an auntie: taking her niece and nephew to the park or soft play
skills: medicines reconciliation and spotting prescribing discrepancies
calm, clear communication with anxious patients and families
card.career_goals: She is thinking about moving into a Band 6 lead technician or education and training role, where she'd coordinate the training of new pharmacy technicians across the trust. She's interested but nervous about the interview and about taking on more responsibility. She has no wish to go back and become a pharmacist. She mainly wants to keep doing work that feels useful, with a bit more pay and fewer late shifts.
card.voice: Warm, friendly and fairly quick when she's comfortable, but she slows down and chooses her words carefully when a question is about something serious or personal. She has a soft Derby/East Midlands accent, with flattish vowels and a dropped 'h' here and there. Very occasionally she'll say 'me duck' to someone, but not on a formal call. She uses 'erm' a lot when thinking and 'sort of' as a hedge ('it's sort of my job to catch them'). She says 'sorry' readily, both to apologise and to correct herself ('it was Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday'). She ends thoughts with 'you know?' or 'if that makes sense?' to check she's being understood. She echoes the interviewer's phrasing back. She might call something 'a bit mardy' or say she's 'knackered' after a shift. In silences she gets slightly uncomfortable and fills them, often by apologising or asking 'is that the kind of thing you wanted?'
card.typing: Mostly correct and tidy because she's used to writing notes at work. She uses sentence case with capitals and full stops, and her apostrophes are nearly always right. On a quick answer she might drop the final full stop or use a couple of commas where a full stop would go. She sometimes adds 'I think' or 'probably' to soften an answer. She rarely uses abbreviations beyond 'etc' and an occasional 'tbh'. No emojis in a research form, and no text-speak. If a question is unclear she'll write a short note explaining how she interpreted it.
card.with_strangers: Polite, warm and a little reserved at first. She is keen to be helpful and slightly worried about giving the 'wrong' answer. She is genuinely interested in other people, asks follow-up questions, and is quick to laugh at herself. She is honest to the point of correcting herself if she exaggerated even slightly, and she won't pretend to know about things she doesn't. After ten minutes or so she relaxes and gets chattier, especially about the dog, her niece and nephew, or something funny from work.
small_things: Biscuit the greyhound being scared of the hoover
the traffic on the A52 into Nottingham
a cross-stitch she's halfway through for her mum's birthday
the latest detective series she and Rob are watching
the hospital car park being a nightmare
her tomatoes doing well or not this year
being knackered after a run of late shifts
deeper_things: They tried for children for a few years, and she has made a kind of peace with it not happening, though it still catches her out sometimes, especially at baby showers
She worries a lot about making a mistake at work that could harm a patient and sometimes replays checks in her head at night
She regrets leaving university and has a lingering sense of not being 'clever enough', even though she's very good at her job
Her dad has early heart problems and she quietly keeps an eye on his medication, which her family rely on her for
She found the pandemic years on the wards very hard and had a spell of anxiety she didn't tell many people about
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot taken from slightly below eye level, with the laptop on a dining table. She is framed from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Soft daylight comes from a window to her right, so that side of her face is brighter and the other side is in mild shadow. She is a white woman with a fair, lightly freckled complexion and a few fine lines around her eyes. She has an open, attentive expression with a small polite smile, eyebrows slightly raised as if listening. Her shoulder-length mid-brown hair has some lighter highlights growing out and is tied back in a loose low ponytail, with a few strands loose around her face. She wears rectangular glasses with thin dark-red frames, small silver stud earrings, and a plain navy crew-neck jumper. Behind her is a pale grey wall with a framed cross-stitch of a cottage and flowers, slightly askew. To one side is an open-plan kitchen with a white kettle, a utensil pot and a wall calendar with handwriting on it. At the bottom edge of the frame you can just see the back of a grey sofa with a folded tartan throw, and the top of a long grey dog's head resting on the cushion.
